mentl/7ce104c:
The banked probe asked which writer leaves the body's row var bound to
empty. It is unify_two_open_records. When two open records with distinct
row vars unify, it computes each side's exclusive fields and binds each
var to the other's, so when both sides know the same fields both extras
are empty and both tails close. Two open rows unifying learn that their
known fields agree and that their remainders are the same unknown; they
never learn there is no remainder. The function's own comment says tails
collapse to one when already linked, and its va == vb arm does exactly
that — the va != vb arm closes instead. It predicts every number this arc
measured: 7, 2 and 15, including the two-known-field case where the
annotation's var takes diff(body, annotation) = [].

The textbook repair went in and the march refused it. One shared fresh
tail, va := TRecordOpen(extra_b, tail) and vb := TRecordOpen(extra_a,
tail), with open_record_full_fields already chasing that shape. Verdict
BROKEN: m2 differs from m3 by 131477 lines and m4 trapped at exit 134
with zero lines. Reverted whole.

The artifact had already recorded why, in the op the change went around.
graph_bind_record_row's comment says the residual lives under its own node
kind because binding residuals under NRowBound made the row slot an
untagged EffRow-or-Ty union every row walk's catch-all silently crossed.
Binding a row handle to a Ty through graph_bind is that union by another
door. I read that comment this turn while locating the op and did not
weigh it against the edit; the march charged for it.

What survives is the useful half: the fix's shape is right — link the
tails, do not close them — and its representation is now constrained to
the row sort, either residual fields plus an unknown-remainder marker in
NRecordRowBound or its own node kind. The reader's existing
NBound(TRecordOpen(...)) arm is not the invitation it looks like.

131477 diff lines is its own measurement: open-record unification with
distinct vars

sonido/7cb1cf3:
Morph was two frozen whole-rig snapshots captured on demand. Adding an
effect after capture left it out of the morph, reordering misaligned A
against B (they were indexed by slot position), and authoring was
all-or-nothing. Replace them with per-effect A/B endpoints keyed to the
graph node id: MorphState stores a value per parameter per pose, seeded
flat (a == b == current) the first time an effect appears, so a new
effect joins the morph immediately and reorder/insert/delete just move
or drop the endpoints that travel with the node. Authoring is
park-and-edit -- focus A or B to park the rig there and record knob
turns into that pose; grab captures the live rig. Wire the
previously-dead per-knob A/B ghost markers through the panel so
participation is visible, tint the effect-panel border to the focused
pose, and add a mode (Ramp/Momentary/Latch) plus an A<->B trigger that
ramps at morph speed.

Add macro auto-assign: an Auto button seeds K1-K6 from the effects in
the chain, one signature parameter each, skipping stepped/read-only/
hidden and the new ParamFlags::MACRO_EXCLUDE (output/mix), with each
knob preset so it reproduces the current value.

Give the web build save/load/export parity with native. The buttons
were compiled out on wasm because rfd's synchronous dialogs are
native-only; use rfd::AsyncFileDialog + spawn_local + a channel drained
in update() so the browser gets a real file picker (load) and download
(save, patch JSON, pedal .bin). USB DFU flash and the CLAP-folder write
stay native -- a browser tab can reach neither.

Persistence format is unchanged; sessions already stored A/B per effect.
Poses are written only when the morph is active, so a flat rig
round-trips byte-identically. Add a regression test that a loaded
session preserves effect order, which is what keeps each pose keyed to
the right effect.

two-top/7cb58b7:
The browser lane's first real run caught a real bug — in the
fingerprint tool, not the sim. Hasher::write_usize emits 4 bytes on
wasm32 and 8 on the 64-bit natives, and std's derived Hash writes enum
discriminants as isize and handles as usize, so every enum-bearing
column diverged from frame 0 while the sim state underneath was
identical. PortableHasher wraps checksum_hasher: fixed-width writes
forward untouched, usize/isize widen to 64-bit. On the natives the
widened bytes are the bytes usize already wrote, so the committed
golden survives unchanged — the golden test proved that before the
browser run did.

The harness swap that made the catch possible: wasm-bindgen-test +
chromedriver + wasm-pack hung identically on two machines without
ever running a test, so the lane now uses the machinery the deployed
site already proved — a wasm-probe feature exports
checksum_golden_probe from the app's own web glue, web/check.html
prints the verdict into the DOM, and wasm.yml greps it out of plain
headless Chrome. Verified locally end to end: CHECKSUMS-OK 1800
frames. The probe feature stays off the deployed site, so visitors
never download the golden.

Wasm logging is now no-subscriber in every profile (the dev branch
was reinstalling the SystemTime-stamping fmt layer under cargo check).
Follow-up, recorded in NORTH_PLAN: bevy_ggrs's own online checksum
hashes components the same derived-Hash way, so browser-vs-phone
netplay needs the same width audit before cross-width duels are real.
noodles/7c5ec94:
Stopped, the app still burned near-playback CPU: feedback loops (the
reverb's sixteen combs, the echo) and always-running LFOs defeat the
browser's silence-skipping, so an idle phone on the session screen
cooked for nothing. The context now suspends six seconds after stop —
past the longest release and reverb tails, so nothing audible can be
clipped — and wakes on any trigger: play, launch, a preview tap, an
editor audition. Suspended is bit-identical silence; the sound cannot
change. Verified live: running while playing, suspended 6 s after
stop, running again the instant a preview fires.

ROADMAP's performance ledger rewritten to match reality: what shipped
across the optimization passes, what remains open (diff-based
repaints, color-mix precompute, committed-change undo snapshots), and
the one fork that stays the builder's call — the always-on chain while
playing is the floor and it IS the sound.

Thom: clips can loop early. Drums, bass, and melody carry a per-clip
step length (2..16); a 12-step bassline now phases against 16-step
drums. The editors get a -/+ length control and dim the steps beyond
the loop; engine indexing is modulo the clip's own length in both
transport modes and the offline render.

Kenny: per-track swing. The transport's built-in swing is retired;
every trigger computes its own offbeat delay from the track's groove
(falling back to the global GROOV), so the hats can sit in a different
pocket than the bass. A groove knob joins amount/motion in the Sound
sheet for drums, bass, and melody.

Chaz: motion rides grow to a 4-bar window. New recordings capture 64
steps (slow sweeps need the room; short rides just repeat inside it),
playback indexes each lane by its own length, and scene-mode tracking
uses a monotonic step counter so multi-bar rides actually advance.

Nigel, plus the builder's own iZotope practice (DECISIONS D7): a
maximizer-style soft-knee ceiling lands between makeup and limiter —
transparent below -4.4 dBFS, tanh into a 0.98 ceiling above. Measured:
every master combo now peaks at -0.2 dBFS instead of overshooting the
limiter by up to +10 dB into DAC hard-clip, RMS within half a dB.

Fred's aspect ships by existing: a voice memo already lands on a track
via the one-shot picker's load-a-wav. The chop deck remains next.
